cases.title: Student's sleep data: preserve the patient pairs
cases.citation: Student (1908). The probable error of a mean. Biometrika 6(1), 1–25; data from Cushny and Peebles (1905).
cases.question: Use a two-sided paired t-test to compare the mean within-patient difference drug_2 minus drug_1, in additional hours of sleep.
cases.unit: One wide row per historical patient, matched using the original R ID.
cases.derivation: Reshape the two ten-value drug vectors by their repeated patient IDs; retain every value. Drug labels are the R labels, with no reconstructed treatment order.
cases.claim_supported: Modern two-sided reanalysis of the paired historical values; reproduce the published mean difference of 1.58 hours.
cases.claim_not_supported: A modern randomized clinical trial, current treatment guidance, or an exact reproduction of Student's historical probability wording.
cases.reference_method: Independent modern SciPy calculation from the preserved values; not an LLM output or original-paper p-value. Two-sided tests; 95% CI; Pearson chi-square correction=False.

cases.title: Berkeley admissions: what pooling conceals
cases.citation: Bickel PJ, Hammel EA, O'Connell JW (1975). Sex bias in graduate admissions: data from Berkeley. Science 187(4175), 398–404.
cases.question: Use Pearson chi-square independence without continuity correction to test the pooled association between sex and admission across these six departments. Department-specific rates are descriptive context.
cases.unit: Source: twenty-four aggregate frequency cells for six departments, not original individual records.
cases.derivation: Preserve all source cells in berkeley_counts.csv. Deterministically repeat each cell by its frequency for the current categorical tool; derived_record_id is a generated label, not an applicant identifier.
cases.claim_supported: Reproduce the six-department pooled association and the department-specific descriptive admission-rate pattern.
cases.claim_not_supported: The original paper's whole-university adjusted significance, a causal account of discrimination, or a universal within-department reversal.
cases.reference_method: Independent modern SciPy calculation from the preserved values; not an LLM output or original-paper p-value. Two-sided tests; 95% CI; Pearson chi-square correction=False.
